summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis via a femoral tunneled catheter, HIV/AIDS on antiretroviral therapy and opportunistic infection prophylaxis, and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was admitted with chills and purulent, tender drainage from her right femoral hemodialysis catheter and lower abdominal pain felt to be referred from the infected tunnel (CT abdomen/pelvis without acute findings). She was treated with antibiotics, had the infected right femoral catheter removed with cultures growing MRSA, and Infectious Disease recommended a prolonged course of vancomycin to be administered with hemodialysis for catheter-related MRSA bacteremia; echocardiography showed no vegetations. Due to complex access and edema, she underwent venography demonstrating significant IVC stenosis and later balloon angioplasty with exchange/replacement of a left femoral tunneled dialysis catheter. Vaginal discharge/burning was treated empirically with a single dose of fluconazole; GC/CT, yeast culture, and bacterial vaginosis testing were negative, and outpatient gynecologic follow-up was advised. She experienced dialysis-associated hypotension/volume depletion after ultrafiltration and was restarted on midodrine, and she was discharged home ambulatory with plans for ongoing dialysis, vancomycin with HD, and outpatient follow-up for dermatologic symptoms and eosinophilia evaluation (Strongyloides testing pending at discharge).
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter (MRSA catheter-related infection)
End stage renal disease on hemodialysis with complex vascular access
Other complications due to renal dialysis device/implant/graft (infected tunneled catheter requiring removal and replacement)
Compression of vein / IVC stenosis requiring venography and balloon angioplasty
Hypotension and volume depletion related to hemodialysis ultrafiltration (midodrine restarted)
Human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] disease with very low CD4; continued ART and OI prophylaxis
Candidiasis/vaginal discharge symptoms (treated with fluconazole; infectious testing negative; needs outpatient GYN follow-up)
Eosinophilia (workup ongoing; Strongyloides antibody pending; consider allergy referral)
Secondary hyperparathyroidism of renal origin (on cinacalcet and phosphate binder)
Herpes zoster with nervous system complications (history; on antiviral therapy)
